newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity securities to trade over Internet.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity securities to trade over Internet.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said individual investors will be able to trade stocks, options and mutual funds over the Internet through brokers and dealers.

Fidelity said its securities clearing unit National Financial will make available a PC-based brokerage service called MAXXinvest which allows securities to be traded through brokers and dealers over the Internet.

Customers will also be able to obtain real-time and delayed quotes, view account positions and balances and access market information such as equity and mutual fund research reports, historical charts and market analysis.
MAXXinvest is a secure, efficient and low-cost system available 24 hours a day, Fidelity said.

"This is a timely introduction of a service that today's retail investors are demanding," said John Post, senior vice president of product development for National Financial. "It makes our discount broker/dealer clients more competitive and opens up new distribution channels for traditional broker/dealers."
Several broker/dealers plan to roll out the system or are evaluating MAXXinvest, Fidelity said.

Tradewell Discount Investing plans to gradually roll out the service over the next few months, Crestar Securities of Richmond, Va., plans to integrate MAXXinvest into its web site in late March and Muriel Siebert & Co of New York is evaluating the system, Fidelity said.
The system uses a firewall, digital certificates, user ID and password protection to ensure security, Fidelity said.
